sources.entry: Element - Element is a collaboration app (currently Electron) for the Matrix protocol.

summary.one_liner: Element Web is a Matrix web and desktop chat client built on the Matrix JS SDK, also packaged as an Electron desktop app.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Element (formerly Vector and Riot) as a Matrix web and desktop client built using the Matrix JS SDK. It can be used in a browser or run as a desktop app wrapped in Electron, with pre-built downloads available or the option to build it yourself. The repository is a monorepo that hosts Element Web and other related projects in subdirectories. The README defines tiers of environment support (supported, best effort, community supported, not supported) covering desktop browsers, Safari, mobile web, and desktop OSes. It also points to the developer guide, code style, contribution guide, and translation docs. For Android and iOS, it recommends the separate native apps element-x-android and element-x-ios.
use_cases: chat on the Matrix protocol in a web browser
run a self-hosted Matrix chat client
use Matrix as a desktop chat app
contribute to the Element Web client
how_to_run: Use the hosted copy of Element at the URL given in the README (the link text is missing from the README).
To host your own instance, follow the 'Installing Element Web' guide referenced in the README.
To install the desktop app, download a pre-built version from the link in the README, or build it yourself using the instructions it references.
notable: Monorepo hosting Element Web and other related projects
Runs as a browser app or as a desktop app wrapped in Electron
Formal tiers of supported environments, from fully supported to not supported
Multi-licensed: AGPL, GPL, or a paid commercial license
Recommends separate native apps for Android and iOS
caveats: Support tiers limit which browsers and OS versions receive fixes; older or unlisted environments are not supported
Android and iOS users are directed to separate native apps rather than this web client
Commercial use outside AGPL or GPL terms requires a paid Element Commercial License
summary.license: AGPL-3.0 or GPL-3.0 (or a paid Element Commercial License)
